variables.name: BirthAsphyxia
variables.description: Binary indicator of perinatal asphyxia, a condition of impaired gas exchange during birth leading to hypoxemia and hypercapnia in the neonate.

variables.name: HypDistrib
variables.description: Categorical indicator characterizing the anatomical distribution pattern of hypoxia in the neonate, distinguishing between generalized and differential (upper vs. lower body) cyanosis.

variables.name: HypoxiaInO2
variables.description: Binary indicator of persistent hypoxemia despite supplemental oxygen administration, suggesting the presence of intracardiac right-to-left shunting or severe pulmonary pathology.

variables.name: CO2
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2), reflecting the adequacy of alveolar ventilation in the neonate.

variables.name: ChestXray
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the radiographic appearance on neonatal chest X-ray, used to identify pulmonary pathology such as ground-glass opacities, hyperinflation, or cardiomegaly.

variables.name: Grunting
variables.description: Binary indicator of expiratory grunting, an audible sign of neonatal respiratory distress caused by partial glottic closure to maintain functional residual capacity and prevent alveolar collapse.

variables.name: LVHreport
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the clinical report documenting the presence or absence of left ventricular hypertrophy based on echocardiographic or electrocardiographic assessment.

variables.name: LowerBodyO2
variables.description: Categorical indicator of transcutaneous oxygen saturation measured at a post-ductal site (lower extremity), used in combination with pre-ductal measurements to assess for differential cyanosis indicative of right-to-left ductal shunting.

variables.name: RUQO2
variables.description: Categorical indicator of transcutaneous oxygen saturation measured at a pre-ductal site (right upper extremity), reflecting systemic arterial oxygenation prior to the ductus arteriosus.

variables.name: CO2Report
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the clinical report documenting the arterial CO2 measurement, reflecting the clinician's interpretation of ventilatory status.

variables.name: XrayReport
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the radiologist's interpretation of the neonatal chest radiograph, summarizing identified pulmonary or cardiac abnormalities.

variables.name: Disease
variables.description: Categorical variable representing the primary neonatal diagnosis, distinguishing among congenital heart disease subtypes, pulmonary pathology, persistent pulmonary hypertension, and normal physiology.

variables.name: GruntingReport
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the clinical report documenting the presence, absence, or severity of expiratory grunting as observed by the clinician.

variables.name: Age
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the neonate's gestational age at birth, distinguishing between preterm, term, and post-term categories, a key determinant of cardiopulmonary maturity.

variables.name: LVH
variables.description: Binary indicator of the presence of left ventricular hypertrophy, characterized by increased left ventricular wall thickness, typically secondary to volume or pressure overload in congenital heart disease.

variables.name: DuctFlow
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the direction and magnitude of blood flow through the ductus arteriosus, distinguishing between left-to-right shunting, right-to-left shunting, and no significant flow.

variables.name: CardiacMixing
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the degree of intracardiac blood mixing, reflecting the presence and severity of shunting through septal defects or other anatomical communications between the systemic and pulmonary circulations.

variables.name: LungParench
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the functional and structural status of the lung parenchyma, reflecting the presence or absence of parenchymal disease such as respiratory distress syndrome, meconium aspiration, or pneumonia.

variables.name: LungFlow
variables.description: Categorical indicator of the volume of blood flow through the pulmonary vascular bed, influenced by pulmonary vascular resistance, cardiac output, and the presence of intracardiac or extracardiac shunts.

variables.name: Sick
variables.description: Binary indicator of the overall clinical severity of the neonate's condition, distinguishing between clinically stable and critically ill presentations requiring intensive care intervention.
